subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — SLOs & sizing

Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — SLOs & sizing

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned before engineering kicks off validation: 

Recap / SLOs you mentioned on the call:
- 95th percentile first-byte latency target: <= 350 ms (streaming start)
- Per-token gen latency target: <= 30 ms/token at p95
- Sustained aggregate throughput target: ~1.5k tokens/sec (expected peak)
- Peak concurrent active requests: 40 (burst to 60 for short windows)
- Streaming required (model must support server-side streaming with chunked start within SLO)

What we need from you to size dedicated capacity properly:
1) Sample payloads (input prompt sizes, typical response lengths) — you mentioned you’d share examples from Prod.
2) Any offline quantization constraints / preference for GPU type (you mentioned H100 preference during the call).
3) Procurement timeline / go-live window.

Proposed next steps:
- If you can drop the sample payloads here, we’ll run an initial sizing matrix (H100 vs A100 options) and propose reserved throughput + canary plan by EOD Wednesday (3/3).
- Engineering (Aditya) will propose a 24–72 hour validation window with soak tests and perf profiles.

Attachments I can prepare: preliminary sizing matrix and a validation test plan once we have sample payloads.

Thanks — looping Marissa and Aditya for visibility.

Best,
Dev Patel
Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Clarifications:
- Our typical prompts average 1.2k tokens input, responses average ~800 tokens (range 200–2k).
- Streaming is critical: customers expect the first chunk within ~300–350ms and then steady streaming at ~18–25 tokens/sec.
- Preferred GPU: H100 (we’re open to A100 if it materially reduces cost, but latency is priority).
- Target go-live: end of Q2; procurement expects to finalize terms by 4/15.

Procurement note (cc’d): we’ll need an official capacity quote and SLA language to move forward.

I’ve attached the payload samples and a short CSV with concurrency profiles. Let me know if you want a small Prod snapshot export — happy to share under an NDA.

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — SLOs & sizing

Alex — great, thanks for the samples. Based on the payloads and your SLOs, here are two sizing options we recommend for a reserved Dedicated pool. I’ll include rough cost and expected headroom — Aditya, please weigh in on the perf assumptions.

Option A — Performance-first (recommended for latency-sensitive workloads)
- GPU: H100 80GB x4 (reserved)
- Expected sustained aggregate throughput: ~1.8k tokens/sec
- Peak concurrency support: 60 concurrent streams with graceful queuing/burst policy
- Expected p95 first-byte latency: 180–320 ms depending on prompt length; per-token gen ~20–28 ms/token
- Canary plan: 1 node (H100) soak + 24h ramp -> full pool ramp over 48 hours
- Notes: supports large context windows and minimal quantization; higher monthly commit cost

Option B — Cost-optimized (quantized)
- GPU: A100 80GB x6 (reserved)
- Expected sustained aggregate throughput: ~1.2k tokens/sec
- Peak concurrency support: 40–50 concurrent streams
- Expected p95 first-byte latency: 300–450 ms; per-token gen ~25–35 ms/token with int8/4-bit quantization
- Canary plan: small A100 pool + performance tuning for quantized kernels

Validation steps we propose (high level):
1) Run synthetic and sample-payload tests for 24–72 hours (soak)
2) Measure first-byte latency (p50/p95/p99), per-token latency, and token/sec across concurrency curves
3) Test streaming startup times and steady-state token throughput (18–25 tps per stream target)
4) Run failover/rollback scenarios and load spikes (burst to 2x expected for 10 minutes)

I’ve attached a draft sizing matrix (dedicated_sizing_matrix.xlsx). If this looks good, Aditya can schedule the validation window for 3/8–3/10 (we can move later if you need more lead time).

Alex — can you confirm which option you prefer (A or B) and if procurement needs a formal quote now?

Thanks,
Dev

Thanks all — forwarding high-level validation plan and test artifacts.

Validation plan (summary):
1) Prep (3/7): stage canary H100 instance with same model binary, load sample payloads, confirm environment parity
2) Canary (3/8): run 24h soak with synthetic + sample payloads at target concurrency (40), collect p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and per-token latencies
3) Scale test (3/9): ramp to full pool (4x H100) and validate aggregate throughput, sustained tokens/sec, and burst tests (2x for 10m)
4) Reliability tests (3/10): simulate node failure, test automatic fallback to reserved variants, verify rollback script

Metrics we will publish:
- p50/p95/p99 first-byte latency (ms)
- per-token gen latency (ms/token)
- aggregate token/sec and tokens/sec per-GPU
- memory/KV-cache utilization and GPU saturation graphs

Artifacts & links:
- Performance validation runbook: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-dedicated-sizing
- Test harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness (internal)
- I’ll push raw logs and summarized report to the shared Drive (post-run).

Attachments: performance-validation-plan.md, raw-benchmark-logs-0310.tar.gz (placeholders)

Notes for Alex: If you confirm Option A (H100 x4), we’ll prioritize latency and aim for p95 < 300 ms across your sample payload mix. If you choose Option B, we’ll include quantization tuning run and provide a side-by-side perf/cost comparison in the final report.

Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
